newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Plutonic shines on large gold find.
newsitem.headline: Plutonic shines on large gold find.

text.p: Shares in gold miner Plutonic Resources Ltd jumped 30 cents or six percent to A$5.50 after the company announced that recent drilling had indicated the discovery of a large new mineable gold deposit in Western Australia.
"It's rallied on the back of this encouraging news," said Eyres Reed dealer Guy Leclezio.
Plutonic said earlier it has made a significant gold discovery near its Darlot gold mine in Western Australia.

"The great thickness of the mineralised zone, its high grade and it apparent continuity over a width of at least 160 metres indicate, even at this early stage of testing, that a large mineable gold deposit has been discovered," Plutonic said.
Plutonic said the discovery, named Darlot Centenary, was open laterally in all directions.
If appreciable lateral extensions are proven a "very substantial gold deposit will be defined," it said.

The vertical step-out drill hole number 362, located 1.2 km east of the existing Darlot gold pit, recently interesected a previously unknown gold mineralised zone, the company said, adding it was seperate ore body from the Darlot pit.

The intersections returned results of 33 metres at 8.0 grams of gold per tonne of ore from 332 metres, 10 metres at 5.2 grams/t from 332 metres and 14 metres at 15.2 grams/t from 351 metres, Plutonic said.
Brokers said the depth and size of the find were good signs.
"It's got a bit of depth to it. There's been a lot of money spent on exploration and Darlot has always looked encouraging," said Leclezio.
